Part two. But back in January 2007, Steve Jobs walked on stage holding a phone with no keyboard at all. His co-CEO, Jim Balsillie, called the iPhone just one more entrant in a crowded market. But people weren't buying the iPhone to type. They bought it for the real web, and soon, for millions of apps. BlackBerry still sold more phones, so it didn't panic. Its first answer was the BlackBerry Storm. Reviewers hated it. Then, in October 2011, the network itself failed. For three days, millions of BlackBerrys couldn't send a message. In 2013, BlackBerry finally launched BlackBerry 10. Six years after the iPhone. Nobody waited for it. In September 2016, BlackBerry stopped making its own phones. And on January fourth, 2022, BlackBerry switched off the service for its classic phones. No data. No texts. Not even calls to nine one one. It failed because it was sure the keyboard would last forever. Follow for more stories like this.
